headline: English rendering of PM’s address during inauguration of Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in Mumbai
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

English rendering of PM’s address during inauguration of Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in Mumbai

08 SEP 2026 8:14PM by PIB Delhi

RBI Governor Shri Sanjay Malhotra ji, Global Fintech Fest Chairman Kris Gopalakrishnan ji, all innovators, leaders and investors of the fintech world, ladies and gentlemen.

I welcome all guests and delegates who have come from India and abroad to the Global Fintech Fest. I am happy that today another hat‑trick has been achieved. One hat‑trick was in 2024 when the government was formed for the third time, and another hat‑trick is my presence among you. This is my third consecutive year at the Global Fintech Fest. This hat‑trick shows how important you are for a developed India, how important your work is.

Every time I come here, I see more youth, I feel more energy. I see the scope of possibilities expanding. It is clear that risk‑taking capacity is increasing, dreams are becoming bolder. And therefore, my confidence in the future of developed India is becoming stronger.

Amidst this energy of fintech, Mumbai is also experiencing cultural energy at its peak these days. In just a few days, Ganeshotsav will begin in Maharashtra and across the country. In our tradition, Lord Ganesh is remembered before every auspicious work. Bowing to Ganapati Bappa, I extend my best wishes to all of you for Global Fintech Fest 2026.

You all know well what the global situation is. The world is passing through a period of conflicts and uncertainty. Energy and commodity supply chains are under pressure, there are tensions in trade. These conditions have persisted for many months. The quarter from April to June was the most challenging. And even in such a situation, when India grows at 7.8 percent, the world gains new confidence. And this trust, I can clearly see on your faces here.

Another example of this growing trust in India is our sovereign ratings. Recently, a Japanese credit rating agency upgraded India’s sovereign ratings to the A category. An upgrade is a matter of happiness, but very few people know that this fortune has come after three decades - after thirty years. This shows how assured the world is about India’s growth momentum, our macro‑economic stability, and the structural reforms carried out in recent years. And I repeat, India’s reform express will move forward at even greater speed.

India’s fintech story has been extraordinary. And one of its biggest champions is our UPI. I spoke about it last year too. But this transformation is so big that whenever fintech is discussed, it will always be incomplete without UPI.

Just a few days ago, on 25th August, UPI completed 10 years. Ten years ago, when I said that your bank would be at your fingertips, some people thought it impossible - and I am talking about well‑informed people, remember their faces. I am not talking about the millions of Indians whose bank accounts had just been newly opened then. Generations of theirs had never even seen the door of a bank. But today, ten years later, look - those same millions of people, who for generations were outside the banking system, have become the big drivers of fintech growth in India.

Today, in the month of August alone, more than 2,400 crore transactions were done through UPI. That means, in just the time we have been sitting here, in 10 minutes alone, on average more than 5 million UPI transactions have taken place across the country. This is the impact because of which France’s President Macron said - he said that UPI is not just a tech story, it is a civilizational story.

UPI is no longer limited to India. A few years ago, if someone had said that payments could be made abroad directly from an Indian bank account, hardly anyone would have believed it. But today, it is a reality. India’s UPI is now live in 11 countries. These are extraordinary figures, showing how long a journey we have traveled. But now the question is - should we be satisfied with this journey? Should we consider fintech’s success in India as final?

I am completing 25 years in the ecosystem of policy and governance. And those who have seen me in these years know - Modi is not one to stop at a milestone, celebrate, and be satisfied. When one goal is achieved, I immediately begin preparing for an even bigger goal.

Today our UPI has reached many countries. But this is only the first step. Our next goal should be to connect with the payment systems of those countries. We have already done this with Singapore. Because of this, transactions between India and Singapore happen just like between two neighborhoods of the same city. This same connection we must build with other countries, other markets. We must move forward with this goal. Wherever Indians live in large numbers, wherever India trades on a large scale, whichever country is ready to walk with us - we must work to connect them all.

This is also necessary because abroad, a large number of Indians work. And Indians are the largest in the world in sending money back home. But today, a part of that money is lost in transaction costs. UPI can save Indians even in this, and money can reach Indian families more quickly.

Today, how do you make payments in India with cards? This system runs on standards that were designed elsewhere. We adopted those standards and rules that others had created. At that time, we did not have our own option. But now we have our own option. Now we can create our own rules and standards, and connect them with the world. I have full confidence in all of you that you can do this.

Technology is the most effective tool of inclusion. And UPI has demonstrated this. When it comes to fintech, its unique feature must be to reach where traditional models could not. Where traditional banks could not reach, where bank branches could not reach, UPI has taken the banking system to that place, to that person.

Today, a large part of the fintech market is only payments. But now we must move to the next level, and move quickly. In the fintech market, along with payments, the share of credit transactions must increase, the share of insurance must increase, the share of savings, investments, and pensions must increase.

I believe fintech can bring out that strength of the country which is still outside the reach of traditional financial models, or not being addressed properly. For a developed India, bringing out this strength is very necessary.

We can already see the impact of this in the success of PM SVANidhi. Our street vendors are the backbone of cities. But they were outside the country’s banking system, outside the formal credit system. PM SVANidhi connected millions of street vendors to the formal system. And now these companions also have the SVANidhi credit card - that means they have a tool of formal credit access. And studies show that the average annual income of these beneficiaries has increased by more than 20 percent. Not only this, their families have seen improvements in housing, nutrition, healthcare access, and children’s education. That is why the government has decided to extend this scheme until 2030.

PM SVANidhi would not have achieved this success if UPI did not exist. UPI has played a very big role in the success of this scheme. Learning from this experience, we must use the power of fintech to further increase economic activities. Let me give you an example from the world of capital and credit. There is a sister who runs a small shop. She receives digital payments every day. Now her income and expenses show a clear pattern. Her business is running well. She has moved beyond the level where small capital was enough. Now she needs goods, equipment to scale up her business, and for this she needs a little more money. This is not very large credit. And her business is still so small that traditional credit models cannot serve her efficiently. There are many such businesses whose needs fintech can analyze, anticipate, and address. And the number of such businesses is very large.

Technology can help us study the economic activities of such businesses and design curated models for them. I believe the next chapter of fintech will be written here. We have shown speed and scale in payments. Now we must help increase the share of non‑payment transactions. For example, a delivery partner, or a person doing some small work - he earns every month, but he needs access to services like savings and pension products. Fintech can address the needs of such people. Similarly, fintech can make access easier to insurance products and other financial services. All these can be made just as simple, easy, and accessible as making a payment today with a QR code.

The first quarter of the 21st century has ended. Now we are in the year 2026. The second quarter has brought even newer possibilities for us. Agentic AI, tokenization, quantum - such technologies are opening new doors of possibilities in the financial sector. Now the challenge before us is how to turn these possibilities into real impact. And for this, I want our fintech companies to set some tasks for themselves. And I want to place some suggestions before you. First - we must make cyber security in India top‑notch. Second - our industry must have its own ethical data protection standards. Third - we must build a strong fintech regulator‑industry innovation ecosystem. And fourth - we must have a fintech consumer protection index, on the basis of which every company can have a transparent rating. If we test ourselves on these parameters, India’s fintech sector can become the gateway of countless possibilities. We have the experience, and we have the way to implement it on the ground. Therefore, we must work quickly.

The success story of Digital India is now ready for a new chapter. The success of our fintech story so far has been scale, scope, secure systems, democratization of technology, and public trust. Keeping these core values in mind, the fintech sector must focus on next‑generation innovation. With this appeal, once again I extend my best wishes to all of you. Thank you very much.

headline: Ministry of Cooperation Restores CRCS-Sahara Refund Portal to Expedite Genuine Depositors’ Claims
fullText:
Ministry of Cooperation

Ministry of Cooperation Restores CRCS-Sahara Refund Portal to Expedite Genuine Depositors’ Claims

Rs 9,267 crore refunded to 41.56 lakh depositors through Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts

Sahara depositors refund process remains secure, transparent, digital, paperless and verification-based

The Ministry of Cooperation restarts processing of claims of depositors of Sahara

08 SEP 2026 8:10PM by PIB Delhi

Guided by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahakar se Samriddhi’ under the leadership of the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah the Ministry of Cooperation and its institutions are dedicated to protecting the interests of cooperative members and strengthening public confidence in the cooperative sector. As part of this commitment, the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS), continues to facilitate payment of eligible and genuine dues to legitimate depositors of Sahara through a secure, transparent and online mechanism, in accordance with the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s order dated 29 March 2023 in W.P. No. 191/2022.

Till date, a total amount of Rs 9,267 crore has been refunded to 41,56,711 depositors directly into their Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts. Approximately 20 lakh applications are still remaining for processing through the CRCS-Sahara Refund Portal. With the portal now restored, verification and refund processing of these pending applications has resumed.

The functioning of the Sahara cooperative societies was affected in November 2025 after their premises were sealed due to certain matters disconnected to the Sahara societies. The Societies also faced operational and administrative constraints, including outstanding dues related to hardware and Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs), renewal of essential IT infrastructure and licenses, and human-resource and other administrative issues. Collectively, these factors disrupted the systems required for verification and processing of refund claims.

The Ministry of Cooperation played a pivotal role in addressing the administrative, financial, operational and technology-related impediments of the Sahara Societies affecting the refund mechanism. Through sustained institutional intervention and coordination with stake holders including the officials and Authorities of Govt of Uttar Pradesh, the CRCS facilitated resolution of the hurdles relating to essential systems, infrastructure and administrative functioning, enabling restoration of the portal and its associated verification systems. This has restarted the processing of legitimate dues of genuine depositors of the Sahara Group cooperative societies, namely, Sahara Credit Cooperative Society Ltd., Lucknow; Saharayn Universal Multipurpose Society Ltd., Bhopal; Humara India Credit Cooperative Society Ltd., Kolkata; and Stars Multipurpose Cooperative Society Ltd., Hyderabad.

The refund process is being administered by the CRCS through the CRCS-Sahara Refund Portal, ensuring that the entire mechanism remains transparent, digital, paperless and verification-based. The dedicated online portal, launched by the Government on 18 July 2023, enables depositors to submit refund applications without physical paperwork, making the process accessible and convenient while maintaining a clear digital trail.

Claims are processed through Aadhaar e-KYC and by matching depositor, membership and account details with data provided by the respective societies. Deposit certificates or receipts and other prescribed documents are scrutinised in accordance with the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) approved under the Supreme Court-directed monitoring mechanism. Upon successful verification, eligible refund amounts are credited directly to the depositor’s Aadhaar-seeded bank account.

The Ministry of Cooperation and the CRCS have taken concerted steps to strengthen the required IT infrastructure, renew essential systems and licenses, clear the operational impediments and address the human-resource and administrative issues that had affected claim processing. The restoration of the portal reflects the Ministry’s people-centric approach and the CRCS’s continuing institutional responsibility to facilitate smooth verification and processing of pending applications while safeguarding the interests of genuine depositors.

Depositors are advised to use only the official CRCS-Sahara Refund Portal (https://mocrefund.crcs.gov.in) for submission of fresh claim and to Resubmission portal (https://mocresubmit.crcs.gov.in) for rectification of errors in submitted claims, whenever communicated and to follow the prescribed process and document requirements while submitting or re-submitting their claims. This will help ensure timely verification and protect applicants from unauthorised channels or misleading claims.

headline: Union Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary says that literacy and education must be reimagined as instruments of empowerment and active citizenship
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Union Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary says that literacy and education must be reimagined as instruments of empowerment and active citizenship

ULLAS is empowering learners with confidence, dignity and opportunities for meaningful participation in society - Shri Jayant Chaudhary

Union Ministry of Education celebrates International Literacy Day 2026 in New Delhi

08 SEP 2026 8:05PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development & Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, today said that ULLAS was empowering learners with confidence, dignity and opportunities for meaningful participation in society. He added that the values of risk-taking and creativity must be inculcated in children to build a strong nation. The Minister was speaking at the national-level celebration of International Literacy Day 2026 in New Delhi.

The Minister emphasised the need to reimagine literacy and education as instruments of empowerment, creativity, dignity and active citizenship. He said that literacy must go beyond the ability to read and write and should encompass comprehension, application of knowledge, financial literacy and digital literacy. He stressed that education must ultimately contribute to sustainable development, economic well-being and the creation of active and responsible citizens.

Shri Chaudhary further emphasised on the importance of nurturing curiosity, critical thinking and creativity among learners, noting that education should equip young people not only with knowledge but also with the confidence and ability to apply it meaningfully in a rapidly changing world. He called upon students, educators and citizens to think differently, question the status quo and contribute creatively towards building a new India.

Speaking on the occasion, Chief Minister of Tripura, Prof. (Dr.) Manik Saha, said that the collective efforts of the State helped Tripura achieve a 95.6% literacy rate, crossing the Government of India’s benchmark for being declared fully literate. He added that the State Government was committed to reducing dropout rates to the minimum possible level within the next three to four years.

Minister of Education, Himachal Pradesh, Shri Rohit Thakur; Minister of Education, Uttarakhand, Dr. Dhan Singh Rawat; Minister of Education and ICT Department, Mizoram, Dr. Vanlalthlana; and Minister of School, Higher and Technical Education, Sikkim, Shri Raju Basnet were the Guests of Honour on the occasion. Secretary, Department of School Education & Literacy (DOSEL), Shri T. K. Anil Kumar; Additional Secretary, DOSEL, Ms. Archana Sharma Awasthi and senior officials of the Ministry participated in the celebration.

The Event was organised as part of the two-day celebration of International Literacy Day 2026, under the aegis of the Department of School Education & Literacy, focusing on the theme for this year, “Literacy for people, the planet and prosperity”. An ULLAS Mela will be organised tomorrow at the National Bal Bhawan. It will bring together participants from 29 States/UTs and provide a national platform for neo-literates, volunteer teachers, and other stakeholders to share their experiences, achievements, innovations and best practices.

The Union Ministry of Education is organising Literacy Fortnight from September 1-14, 2026 across the country with a host of activities including workshops, seminars, gram panchayat-level programmes, rallies, nukkad nataks, registration drives, social media campaigns and other outreach initiatives. The campaign will facilitate mass participation thereby inculcating a sense of ‘Kartavyabodh’ and ‘Janbhagidari’ in all citizens. This will in turn help attain the goal of making India fully literate under the vision of ULLAS - Nav Bharat Saakasharta Karyakam. The campaign will reaffirm the collective commitment towards achieving the vision of “Jan Jan Saakshar” and building a society where every individual has opportunities for foundational literacy and lifelong learning.

headline: From Skilled Worker to Swachhta Udyami: Diwakar Kumar's Journey towards Self-Reliance

Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Skilled Worker to Swachhta Udyami: Diwakar Kumar's Journey towards Self-Reliance

08 SEP 2026 8:04PM by PIB Delhi

Empowered by Education, Inspired to Serve: Dr. M. K. Ponselvakumari’s Journey from Doctoral Research to Professional Success

Higher education and research open pathways for knowledge, innovation and service to society. For committed scholars, timely fellowship assistance can provide the academic stability and research resources required to translate ambition into achievement.

Demonstrating the positive impact of support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme, Dr. M. K. Ponselvakumari, a 34-year-old scholar from Karaikal district in Puducherry, successfully completed her Ph.D. and is now employed full-time. Her journey reflects determination, academic commitment and the enabling role of institutional support in advancing doctoral research and professional aspirations.

Before receiving assistance under the NFSC Scheme, Dr. Ponselvakumari encountered challenges in meeting the specialised requirements of doctoral research. Conducting experiments required research materials, access to different laboratories and external analytical facilities. Managing the associated expenditure while pursuing higher studies made it difficult to maintain continuity in her research work.

Accessibility between laboratories presented an additional practical barrier. The need to use specialised facilities and outsource certain analyses required both mobility and adequate resources. These circumstances also created uncertainty and mental pressure during an academically demanding phase of her journey.

Despite these challenges, Dr. Ponselvakumari remained focused on completing her Ph.D. and building a meaningful professional career. Her aspiration was to join the Agricultural Research Service (ARS) and contribute through research, knowledge and public service.

During 2017–18, Dr. Ponselvakumari began receiving assistance under the NFSC Scheme in the form of fellowship and contingency support. The assistance enabled her to procure essential research materials, undertake outsourced analyses and meet expenditure connected with her research and paper publication.

The fellowship addressed several of the practical challenges that had affected her doctoral work. Access to contingency support helped her plan experiments, obtain the necessary materials and use analytical services with greater confidence. It also eased the mental burden associated with arranging resources and enabled her to concentrate more fully on the quality and progress of her research.

With sustained support under the NFSC Scheme, Dr. Ponselvakumari successfully completed her Ph.D. The achievement represented an important academic milestone and strengthened her prospects for professional advancement. She is now a full-time employee, reflecting the positive transition from doctoral scholar to an independent professional.

Dr. Ponselvakumari acknowledges the significant role of the fellowship in her journey and expresses her gratitude to the Ministry for supporting her doctoral studies. For her, the assistance was instrumental in completing research activities, procuring materials and publishing academic work that formed an essential part of her Ph.D.

Her journey highlights how timely fellowship and contingency assistance can expand access to advanced education, strengthen research capability and enable scholars to pursue their aspirations with confidence. Dr. Ponselvakumari’s success stands as an example of academic perseverance supported by opportunity, empowerment and institutional encouragement.

New Delhi, September 8, 2026: The Indian contingent for the Asian Games 2026 received a grand send-off in New Delhi today in the presence of Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya.

Dr. Mandaviya, along with Indian Olympic Association (IOA) President Dr. P.T. Usha, Secretary (Sports) Hari Ranjan Rao and Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav, unveiled the official contingent jersey ahead of the Games in the presence of athletes and support staff.

“I have complete faith that our contingent will perform well at the Asian Gaes and increase the pride of the country,” he said.

He expressed confidence in the performance of the Indian contingent, saying, “Sports is a sector where success is not just a matter of pride for the athlete alone – the athlete’s success is the nation’s success. headline: NCSC Issues Notice to Punjab Government Over Death of Sangrur Resident Gulzar Singh
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

NCSC Issues Notice to Punjab Government Over Death of Sangrur Resident Gulzar Singh

Commission Seeks Detailed Report Within Five Days

Chairman to Visit Sangrur on 10 September 2026

08 SEP 2026 7:49PM by PIB Delhi

The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) has issued a notice to the Punjab Government in connection with the death of Gulzar Singh, a resident of Sangrur district of the State of Punjab.

According to the complaint received by the Commission, Gulzar Singh had raised questions before the Finance Minister of Punjab regarding the problem of narcotic substances in the State. In a video circulated on social media before his death, he reportedly claimed that he had consumed poison due to fear of the Minister and also levelled serious allegations against certain members of the village panchayat.

Exercising the powers conferred upon it under Article 338 of the Constitution of India, the Commission ordered inquiry into the matter. The notices have been issued to the Chief Secretary and the Director General of Police, Government of Punjab, directing them to submit the facts of the case and a report on the action taken regarding the allegations within five days of receipt of the notice.

The Commission initiated action on a complaint filed by Shri Sheetal Angural, former MLA and State President, BJP SC Morcha, Punjab.

NCSC Chairman Shri Kishor Makwana described the matter as an extremely serious and sensitive incident. He said that allegations made against a Minister and certain members of the village panchayat by name in a video recorded before the death warranted an impartial, independent and high-level inquiry.

Shri Makwana said that a detailed report has been sought from the Punjab Government. He also announced that he will visit Sangrur on 10 September 2026 to examine the matter and ascertain the veracity of the allegations.

He added that the Commission remains committed to ensuring justice for the family of the deceased and safeguarding the constitutional rights of members of the Scheduled Castes.

headline: Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister of Coal & Mines, Launches First-Ever Sector-Wide CSR Framework for Indian Coal Companies; Celebrates Milestones under Thalassemia Bal Sewa Yojana and Nanha Sa Dil
fullText:
Ministry of Coal

Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister of Coal & Mines, Launches First-Ever Sector-Wide CSR Framework for Indian Coal Companies; Celebrates Milestones under Thalassemia Bal Sewa Yojana and Nanha Sa Dil

Over 1,050 Bone Marrow Transplants and 1,500 Corrective Cardiac Surgeries Completed under CIL's Flagship CSR Schemes

08 SEP 2026 7:48PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Coal, along with Coal India Limited (CIL), today celebrated key milestones under its flagship Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives — the Thalassemia Bal Sewa Yojana (TBSY) and Nanha Sa Dil — and launched the Comprehensive CSR Framework for Indian Coal Companies, at an event held at New Delhi.

The event was graced by Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister for Coal and Mines, and Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines, along with Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, Secretary to the Govt. of India, Ministry of Coal, in the presence of senior officials, medical experts, implementing partners, and beneficiary families.

Thalassemia Bal Sewa Yojana (TBSY)

Launched to address the treatment needs of children suffering from Thalassemia and Aplastic Anaemia — rare genetic blood disorders — TBSY has grown from an initial network of 4 hospitals to 21 empanelled hospitals across the country. CIL is the only Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) in India to have undertaken a healthcare initiative of this scale for rare genetic blood disorders such as Thalassemia and Aplastic Anemia. Under the scheme, up to Rs. 10 lakh per patient is extended directly to empanelled hospitals for Bone Marrow Transplant (BMT), against a total outlay of Rs. 130 crore across four phases. To date, more than 1,050 BMTs have been completed, with the overwhelming majority of treated children now leading normal, healthy lives. The scheme is implemented in coordination with Thalassemics India, with monitoring guidance from the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

Addressing Congenital Heart Defects (CHD), which affect an estimated 2.4 lakh newborns in India annually — of whom only about 5 percent receive timely treatment — Nanha Sa Dil was launched by CIL in partnership with the Sri Sathya Sai Health and Education Trust. Beginning with four districts of Jharkhand in March 2024 by CIL, the initiative has since been scaled up through CIL's subsidiary companies SECL, CCL, NCL and WCL. Over 2 lakh children have been screened using modern diagnostic tools, and more than 1,500 corrective surgeries have been completed, entirely free of cost to patient families, including travel and hospitalisation expenses.

Comprehensive CSR Framework for Indian Coal Companies

Marking a significant step towards outcome-oriented CSR, the Ministry of Coal launched CSR framework for coal sector, the first sector specific CSR framework since the advent of statutory CSR under the Companies Act, 2013. The framework has been prepared by the Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA) and serves as a guiding framework for an impactful and outcome oriented CSR for benefit of people residing in the coal mining areas.

Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister of Coal and Mines highlighted Coal India’s sustained CSR commitment over the past decade on healthcare, education, livelihoods and community development. He lauded key initiatives including the Thalassemia Bal Sewa Yojana, Nanha Sa Dil and SECL’s Sushrut. He asserted the importance of whole of society approach including from central and state governments, implementing agencies and parents’ associations for benefit of children suffering from Thalassemia and Congenital Heart Disease. He also assured support for educational needs for brighter future of beneficiary children.

Minister of State for Coal & Mines, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, said that every child should have access to better treatment, essential healthcare facilities and the opportunity to lead a dignified life. He appreciated the efforts of Coal India Limited (CIL) through its CSR initiatives to support thalassemia treatment and affected families.

Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, Secretary, Ministry of Coal, in his address highlighted the transformative impact of Coal India’s CSR initiatives in bringing life-saving healthcare to children and families in need. He appreciated the selfless contribution of doctors, empanelled hospitals and partner organisations, and highlighted quality-assured care, real-time case tracking, transparency, accountability and scalability as key strengths of these initiatives.

Delivering the welcome address Ms. Rupinder Brar, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Coal, highlighted that the true spirit of CSR lies in touching lives, empowering communities and creating opportunities for those who need them the most. She underlined the importance of ensuring that CSR interventions are rooted in local needs, backed by thoughtful planning and measured through tangible outcomes. The new framework, she noted, is an important step towards making CSR more structured, transparent and impact-oriented across the coal sector, ensuring that every initiative translates into real benefits on the ground and contributes to stronger, healthier and more empowered communities.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr Shantanu Sen, Head of Transplant Unit, Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital, Mumbai highlighted that more than 10,000 kids in India are born with Thalassemia every year. He said that their entire life is spent getting blood transfusion. Despite this, he said that many of these kids won’t survive for long. The only cure existing for this is Bone Marrow Transplant, he added. Biggest challenge parents of these kids face is the expensive nature of BMT. He thanked Coal India on behalf of the medical fraternity for making this very expensive treatment available through this very innovative, lifesaving and unique program, called Thalassemia Bal Seva Yojana.

The beneficiary children and their families also expressed their heartfelt gratitude to Coal India Limited, the Ministry of Coal, the doctors, hospitals and partner organisations for the support extended to them. Sharing their personal journeys, the children spoke about how timely treatment had given them renewed hope, confidence and an opportunity to look forward to a brighter future. Their words and smiles reflected the real impact of CSR—not merely in numbers or projects, but in lives transformed, dreams restored and futures made brighter.

The event also featured the release of a book on TBSY, screening of short films on CIL's CSR initiatives in health sector, felicitation of doctors and distinguished dignitaries, and interactions with beneficiary families.

Secretary MeitY: Availability of high-quality data is fundamental to the successful deployment of AI for governance

Secretary, MoSPI: Harmonised, quality-assured and well-documented data is fundamental to an AI-ready government

08 SEP 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) organized a Workshop of Statistical Advisers (SAs) and Chief Data Officers of all Central Government Ministries, Departments and Organisations (MDOs) on September 08, 2026 at Rang Bhawan Auditorium, Akashwani Bhawan, Broadcasting House, Parliament Street, New Delhi – 110001 on the theme “Data Harmonisation for Use of Administrative Data in Data Driven Governance.” The workshop was aimed at strengthening the National Data System, promoting effective use and harmonisation of administrative data, and fostering greater coordination for data-driven governance and evidence-based policymaking across Government.

The inaugural session was graced by Shri Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI and Shri P. R. Meshram, Director General (Data Governance), MoSPI. The meeting was attended by Statistical Advisers, Chief Data Officers as well as other senior officers and other representatives from various Central Ministries/Departments of Government of India.

The Chief Guest, Shri Shaktikanta Das launched the Quarterly Progress Report (QPR) portal on Data Harmonisation (https://qpr.mospi.gov.in). The QPR Portal is a technology-enabled platform for use by all Central MDOs to report progress in identification and cataloguing of datasets made ready for dissemination, its metadata preparation, use of national and international standards, classifications and common unique identifiers in machine readable data, and performing quality checks as per Statistical Quality Assurance Framework (SQAF) by respective MDO. The QPR portal has automated validation, dashboards, cross-verification with the NMDS web portal and shall provide analytical insights across Ministries, Departments and Organisations

In his Keynote address, Shri Shaktikanta Das emphasised that trusted, timely and interoperable data is essential for evidence-based policymaking and data-driven governance. He called for greater use of administrative data and statistical expertise across Ministries/Departments for policy formulation, monitoring and outcome assessment. Key MoSPI initiatives, including NMDS 2.0, SQAF, statistical classifications, data lifecycle guidelines, e-Sankhyiki, Microdata Portal and QPR on Data Harmonisation, were highlighted as important enablers of a stronger administrative data ecosystem. He urged all Ministries/Departments to establish Data Governance Committees, publish data-sharing frameworks, maintain live dataset inventories and leverage existing national data-sharing platforms such as API Setu, data.gov.in, NDAP, AI Kosh, DigiLocker, Entity Locker, e-Sankhyiki and microdata portal. He stressed the need for a whole-of-government approach to build a modern, integrated, responsive and future-ready data ecosystem in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Shri S. Krishnan highlighted the importance of effective data sharing, harmonization and interoperability across Ministries/Departments to strengthen evidence-based policymaking and improve governance. It was emphasized that the availability of high-quality data is fundamental to the successful deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for governance. He emphasized optimal utilization of government data in view of rapid digitization and the increasing availability of administrative data. Efforts should focus on utilizing such data effectively for improved welfare outcomes, policy formulation and delivery of government services. Whole-of-government approach should be adopted. Existing resources, including statistical officers, India AI Mission experts, NIC personnel and other data professionals working across Ministries/Departments, should be leveraged.

Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, while setting the context for the meeting, underscored the need to move from siloed departmental data systems towards an integrated, interoperable and government-wide data ecosystem to support the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. He emphasised harmonisation of concepts, definitions, classifications, identifiers, geographies, metadata and data structures for effective data utilisation. He highlighted the complementary roles of Statistical Advisers in statistical leadership and quality assurance and Chief Data Officers in data governance and interoperability, supported by the National Data Governance Committee and the QPR on Data Harmonisation. He stressed a “data discovery before data request” approach, noting that harmonised, quality-assured and well-documented data is fundamental to an AI-ready government. He called for continuous harmonisation, proactive data sharing and collective ownership of data as a national asset.

Shri P. R. Meshram, Director General (Data Governance), MoSPI, delivered the welcome address and highlighted the importance of data harmonisation and interoperability for strengthening data-driven governance and enabling effective use of administrative data across Government Ministries and Departments. The need to move beyond conventional data sharing towards common definitions, metadata, classifications, identifiers and interoperable systems was highlighted. The complementary roles of Statistical Advisors and Chief Data Officers (CDOs) in ensuring statistical quality, data governance and responsible data management were emphasised. He highlighted the importance of making data AI ready and machine readable. The road ahead is moving from structural interoperability to semantic interoperability, from isolated datasets to interoperable and linked data ecosystems, and from data availability to data readiness.

The technical sessions featured presentations on Data Harmonisation through the NMDS and QPR Portals; Model Data Sharing Framework and digital data-sharing mechanisms; institutional approaches to breaking data silos; AI-ready data ecosystems; Data DHARA methodology; India’s Digital Public Infrastructure; UPYOG; health data; and preparation of thematic and extended accounts to measure the contribution of an MDO in the economy.

The presentations highlighted how India can strengthen harmonisation, sharing and use of administrative data disseminated by any Ministry for AI-ready, data-driven governance by all Ministries. MoSPI showcased key initiatives including NMDS 2.0, SQAF, common identifiers and the QPR Portal, while MeitY presented the Model Data Sharing Framework and digital platforms for secure data sharing. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs demonstrated API-based interoperability, including beneficiary-validation use cases. National Urban Digital Mission and Government of NCT of Delhi’s Data DHARA highlighted the potential of harmonized data for real-time urban governance and improved service delivery. Other sessions covered interoperable cross-border trade data, AIKosh, health-data harmonisation, and MoSPI’s transition to the SNA 2025 framework. A key message was that data need not be centralised to generate value; use of common standards, common unique identifiers, APIs and governance mechanisms can enable interoperability across distributed data systems. The discussions emphasised the importance of preserving departmental ownership while ensuring privacy, security and responsible data sharing.

The workshop reaffirmed the commitment of MoSPI and participating Ministries/Departments to build a modern, harmonised, interoperable and data-driven National Data System for evidence-based governance.

headline: India highlights major expansion of medical, nursing and allied healthcare workforce; reaffirms commitment to equitable access to specialized care for rural, tribal and underserved populations at WHO RC79

Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

India highlights major expansion of medical, nursing and allied healthcare workforce; reaffirms commitment to equitable access to specialized care for rural, tribal and underserved populations at WHO RC79

Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Addresses Ministerial Roundtable at 79th WHO Regional Committee Session

Medical Colleges More Than Double Since 2014; MBBS and PG Seats Rise by Over 175%: Shri J.P. Nadda

WHO South-East Asia Region Adopts Dili Declaration on Equity in Specialized Care

WHO Recognises India’s Sustained Leadership in Maternal Health and Noncommunicable Disease Management; honoured with Two WHO South-East Asia Regional Awards

08 SEP 2026 7:01PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, participated in the Ministerial Roundtable on “Human Resources for Health: Equity in Specialized Care” held during the 79th Session of the WHO Regional Committee for South-East Asia (RC79) in Timor-Leste. The Roundtable brought together Health Ministers and senior representatives of Member States of the WHO South-East Asia Region to deliberate on strengthening health workforce capacity and ensuring equitable access to specialized healthcare.

Addressing the Roundtable, Shri J.P. Nadda emphasized that equitable access to specialized care is integral to achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and requires a comprehensive approach encompassing education and training, deployment, retention and continuing professional development of the healthcare workforce.

The Union Health Minister highlighted India's significant progress in expanding its health workforce capacity and strengthening access to specialized healthcare, particularly for people living in rural, tribal, underserved and hard-to-reach areas.

Shri Nadda highlighted that the Government of India has significantly expanded medical education infrastructure through the establishment of new medical colleges and upgradation of existing Government Medical Colleges, resulting in a substantial increase in undergraduate and postgraduate medical seats.

Since 2014, the number of medical colleges in the country has more than doubled from 387 to 858, registering an increase of 121.71 per cent. During the same period, MBBS seats have increased from 51,348 to 1,42,464, an increase of 177.45 per cent, while postgraduate seats have risen from 31,185 to 86,287, an increase of 176.69 per cent.

The Minister also highlighted the targeted expansion of postgraduate capacity. The schemes for increasing medical seats were extended in September 2025, with a target of creating 10,000 additional postgraduate seats by 2028–29, with priority accorded to underserved areas and shortage specialities such as Emergency Medicine, Geriatrics, Psychiatry and Family Medicine.

Highlighting the importance of a strong and diversified healthcare workforce, Shri Nadda stated that 157 new nursing colleges are being established co-located with existing medical colleges. These institutions are expected to add approximately 15,700 nursing graduates annually, with particular emphasis on improving access to quality and affordable nursing education in underserved districts and States/Union Territories.

He further noted that Nurse Practitioner Programmes have been introduced in 10 critical specialities, supported by the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission Act, 2023.

The Union Minister also highlighted India's efforts to expand the allied and healthcare workforce. The Government has announced the creation of 1,00,000 allied and healthcare professionals over five years, supported by the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021 and the establishment of the National Commission in 2024. The Commission brings 57 diverse allied and healthcare professions within a structured regulatory framework.

Shri Nadda highlighted the role of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in providing comprehensive primary healthcare, including screening, early identification and referral services. Ayushman Arogya Shivirs further extend screening and specialist consultations to underserved communities.

He also highlighted the role of Community Health Centres and First Referral Units in providing specialist and referral services. To improve the availability and retention of specialists in difficult areas, India is adopting flexible mechanisms including competitive remuneration, difficult-area allowances, in-sourcing of speciality services, performance-based incentives and fixed-tenure postings.

The Union Minister emphasized that India is leveraging digital health technologies to overcome geographical barriers and extend access to specialist services. Platforms such as eSanjeevani and ABHA-enabled digital health records are facilitating teleconsultation, referrals and continuity of care, particularly for populations in remote and underserved areas.

Shri Nadda underscored that India's approach is moving towards building a larger, more diverse and geographically well-distributed health workforce, with sustained emphasis on underserved areas and shortage specialities. He highlighted that these measures reflect a team-based and continuum-of-care approach to advancing equity in specialized care.

A key outcome of RC79 was the adoption of the “Dili Declaration on Human Resources for Health: Equity in Specialized Care” by the Health Ministers of Member States of the WHO South-East Asia Region.

Through the Declaration, Member States have committed to a comprehensive set of actions aimed at addressing health workforce shortages, maldistribution and the growing need for specialized healthcare.

The Declaration calls for aligning health workforce planning, education and financing with current and future demographic, epidemiological and health emergency preparedness needs. It also calls for policies to attract, recruit, deploy, retain and improve the performance of specialist health workers, particularly in rural and underserved areas, guided by the WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel.

The Declaration further emphasizes optimizing the existing workforce through task-sharing, mentoring, rotational outreach and visiting specialist programmes, including collaboration with qualified and registered Traditional, Complementary and Integrated Medicine practitioners.

Member States have also committed to strengthening integrated referral systems and continuity of care through primary healthcare teams, specialist outreach services, teleconsultation networks and coordinated referral hospitals.

The Declaration calls for strengthening public health workforce capacity and essential public health functions, while accelerating the safe and equitable adoption of digital health technologies, including telemedicine, teleconsultation and AI-supported clinical tools, to expand access to specialist services for rural, remote and underserved populations.

It further promotes innovative service delivery models, including mobile and outreach specialist teams and community-based specialist care, with integration of Traditional, Complementary and Integrated Medicine services.

The Member States also agreed to integrate palliative care into health systems at all levels through workforce development, multidisciplinary teams, community-based services and strengthened referral pathways.

The Declaration emphasizes strengthening national capacity for high-priority specialized services, including cancer, cardiovascular care, trauma, maternal and newborn care, mental health, geriatric care and rehabilitative care. It also calls for strengthening national health workforce information systems to support evidence-based policy-making.

Recognizing the importance of regional cooperation, Member States committed to facilitating information exchange, joint training, clinical mentorship and regional collaboration, including through a regional network of health professional regulators and policy-makers.

The Dili Declaration recalls the commitments made under the 2023 Delhi Declaration on strengthening primary healthcare and responds to the Region's rapid demographic and epidemiological transition, rising burden of complex and chronic conditions, and persistent shortages and maldistribution of specialist health workers.

Member States called upon the World Health Organization to support implementation of the commitments through technical assistance, capacity-building, policy guidance and strengthened regional collaboration mechanisms.

India welcomed the adoption of the Dili Declaration as a significant step towards ensuring equitable access to specialized care, advancing Universal Health Coverage and realizing Health for All across the South-East Asia Region. India reaffirmed its commitment to working closely with Member States and the WHO to translate the commitments of the Declaration into concrete action.

Furthermore, at the 79th Session of the WHO Regional Committee, India was honoured with two WHO South-East Asia Regional awards, recognising the country's sustained achievements in critical areas of public health.

India received recognition for Sustaining the regional elimination of maternal and neonatal tetanus over the past decade; and Strong leadership in addressing noncommunicable diseases through primary healthcare, including achievement of national targets for placing people on protocol-based management for hypertension and diabetes.

The recognition reflects India's sustained commitment to strengthening primary healthcare, disease prevention, early detection and effective management of priority health conditions.

The Union Health Minister dedicated these recognitions to the frontline health workers across the country, whose unwavering commitment and dedicated service have been instrumental in strengthening India's health system and contributing to improved health outcomes.

The Government of India remains committed to advancing Universal Health Coverage through investments in health infrastructure, human resources, primary healthcare, digital health and health system resilience.

STPI Organises Electropreneur Summit 2026 at IIIT-Delhi

Open Challenge Programme launched; MoUs exchanged with Spoke Centres and Investors to Expand Support for Electronics Innovation and Entrepreneurship

08 SEP 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), a premier S&T organization under the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), organized the STPI Electropreneur Summit 2026 at IIIT-Delhi. The summit brought together government leadership, academic pioneers, and industry stalwarts to deliberate on expanding India’s Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) footprint.

A key highlight of the event was the launch of the Open Challenge Programme of the STPI Electropreneur Park. The programme seeks to identify and support innovative technology solutions and startups in the ESDM domain. On the occasion, MoUs were exchanged between AIC STPINEXT INITIATIVES and Spoke Centres (11 partner institutions spanning Chandigarh, Delhi, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, and Uttarakhand) as well as investors (Indian Angel Network Services Private Limited (IAN) & Solara VC), to strengthen collaboration and expand the reach of the Electropreneur ecosystem. The EP 2.0 Spoke Centres, which will democratize access to ESDM incubation and enable innovators across the region to access incubation, mentoring, infrastructure and ecosystem support, include ACIC RISE, Association Chandigarh; Engineering College, CEC Landran; NSUT Incubation and Innovation Foundation (NSUT-IIF); KR Mangalam Incubation & Entrepreneurship Centre (KEIC Foundation); Manav Rachna University, Faridabad; IIT Mandi Catalyst; NewGen IEDC–Business and Innovation Centre, University of Kashmir; MNIT Innovation and Incubation Centre (MIIC), MNIT Jaipur; AKGEC Skills Foundation; Sharda Launchpad Federation, Sharda University, Greater Noida; Swami Rama Himalayan University, Dehradun; UPES Council for Innovation & Entrepreneurship (UCIE); and Runway Incubator.

The inaugural session commenced with the ceremonial lighting of the lamp following welcome remarks by Mrs. Vandana Srivastava, Director, STPI-Noida. Prominent ecosystem leaders delivered opening addresses, including Shri Pradeep Gupta, CMD of CyberMedia; Shri Ashok Chandak, President of IESA & SEMI India; and Prof. Sandeep Sen, Director of IIIT-Delhi.

Delivering the Special Address, Shri K.K. Singh, Joint Secretary, MeitY, highlighted the importance of innovation and entrepreneurship in advancing India’s ESDM ecosystem and spoke about the initiatives being undertaken by the Ministry to support growth in the sector. He said, “India's technology journey is entering a crucial next stage combining our proven global leadership in software with an aggressive push toward Electronic System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) and semiconductors. EP 1.0 laid a strong foundation, nurturing 59 startups, filing 66 patents, and creating over ₹640 crore in startup valuation. With EP 2.0, we are scaling our ambitions to target 500 startups, expanding deep into Tier-II and Tier-III cities so that talent across every corner of the nation can participate in this growth. Our true benchmark for success will be converting this immense talent into commercialized intellectual property and globally competitive products.”

Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI, in his special address highlighted the objectives of the STPI Electropreneur Summit and the significant transformation in India’s technology and electronics landscape and the growing opportunities for innovators in Deep Tech, AI and Electronic System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM). He said, “Today marks an exciting time for technology in India. Historically, our talent shifted primarily toward software services building a $200B+ export industry while electronics manufacturing lagged. But the landscape has fundamentally changed. Over the past decade, national electronics production grew seven times from under ₹2 lakh crore to over ₹13 lakh crore, while exports surged eleven times to ₹4.24 lakh crore. Speaking about Electropreneur Park, he highlighted its journey and the progress achieved through EP 1.0, which has delivered 129 products, 27 trademarks, 66 patent filings and ₹150 crore in cumulative revenue. Now, with Electropreneur Park 2.0, we are taking this vision to the next level from nurturing 500 startups to building a strong and interconnected ESDM innovation ecosystem across North India. Further, with various other government initiatives i.e. GPU access through the India AI Mission, and the ₹1.275 lakh crore through ISM 2.0 scheme, this is the right time for young innovators to build hardware, design products, and lead global electronics manufacturing.

The afternoon program featured a technical address by Shri S.K. Marwah, Advisor, R&D Electronics Division, MeitY. This set the stage for a panel discussion on "Bridging the Gap: Accelerating ESDM Innovation through Government-Academia-Industry Synergies," moderated by Dr. Anuj Grover, Associate Professor at IIIT-Delhi, along with other panelists Dr. Amjad Hussain, Director - HCIE, SRHU – Dehradun, Shri Rajoo Goel, Secretary General, ELCINA, Shri S.K Marwah, Advisor, R&D Electronics Division, MeitY.

The STPI Electropreneur Summit is a premier initiative by STPI that brings together Electropreneurs, innovators, startups, industry leaders, investors, academia and policymakers to exchange ideas, forge partnerships, unlock opportunities and shape the future of electronics and deep-tech innovation in India. An electropreneur is an entrepreneur who starts, develops, and scales businesses specifically within the electronics and hardware-driven technology sectors.

During the Summit, the Open Challenge Programme (OCP) for the STPI Electropreneur Park was launched, along with the exchange of MoUs with 11 Spoke Centres as well as with investors, including Indian Angel Network Services Private Limited (IAN) and Solara VC.

The Spoke Centres of STPI Electropreneur Park CoE, New Delhi, are partner institutions spanning Chandigarh, Delhi, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand that will facilitate extending the reach of the Electropreneur Park and provide incubation support, mentorship, infrastructure and ecosystem access to innovators and startups in their respective regions.

Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is a premier S&T organization under Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) engaged in promoting IT/ITES Industry, innovation, R&D, start-ups, product/IP creation in the field of emerging technologies like IoT, Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Computer Vision, Robotics, Robotics Process Automation (RPA), Augmented & Virtual Reality, Animation & Visual effect, Data Science & Analytics for various domains like Gaming, FinTech, Agritech, MedTech, Autonomous Connected Electric & Shared(ACES) Mobility, ESDM, Cyber Security, Industry 4.0, Drone, Efficiency Augmentation, etc.

Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

MoSJE Expands Partnerships with Spiritual Organisations under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan

MoUs with Four Spiritual Organisations to be Signed Tomorrow in New Delhi

08 SEP 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, is expanding its collaboration with spiritual organisations under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), advancing the shared vision of building a drug-free India.

Recognizing the vital role of spiritual organisations in guiding communities, instilling discipline and promoting value-based living, the Department has partnered with leading spiritual institutions to strengthen outreach and awareness against substance abuse.

In continuation of this initiative, the Department will sign MoUs with Adhyatm Vigyan Satsang Kendra, Chinmaya Mission, Divya Jyoti Jagrati Sansthan and Hare Krishna Movement. The signing ceremony will be held at the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in the National Capital here tomorrow Wednesday, in the presence of Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, senior officials of the Department and revered spiritual gurus.

Earlier, Memoranda of Understanding were signed with The Art of Living, Brahma Kumaris, Sant Nirankari Mission, ISKCON, Shri Ram Chandra Mission, All World Gayatri Pariwar, Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Dhanwantari Ashram and the University of Patanjali.

These partnerships have supported mass-awareness programmes, volunteer mobilisation and the integration of yoga, meditation and spiritual counselling into de-addiction efforts.
